svg.text: Figure 6.3. The address generator, reader side: GROUP and STREAM read ahead of the timetable
v1.0 (spec/machine-spec.md §4.2, §4.10) — figure 6.4 is the visit side that consumes the two queues
kind (stream run or group run), start, count
group index g = start … start + count − 1
reads GROUP[g], one read per cycle,
while the GROUP queue has a free credit
Group run: for the group at its reader pointer,
R = 0: no reads, the pointer moves on
Stream run: k = 0 … count − 1: read STREAM[start + k]
one read per cycle, while a STREAM credit is free
ag_lookahead entries (4 shown), each the whole
entry: source, cm field, count, d, mode, size, gap after
the head is the current group:
R, t, gap; popped at its end
popped as each visit is made
reader pointer, at or after the head: the STREAM reader's group
credit back when its group ends
credit back when a visit uses its entry
Example: a group run of three groups. The STREAM reads come out in visit order, so the queue is simply consumed from its head.
g0: streams a, b, c (t = 3), R = 2; g1: streams d, e (t = 2), R = 0; g2: streams f, g, h, k (t = 4), R = 1
the GROUP reader runs ahead of the STREAM reader; g1's entry is read but
passed by the reader pointer (no STREAM reads), and takes one cycle on the timetable
• The read order depends only on the entries, never on the data, so both readers run ahead freely; nothing in the visit side feeds back except the credits.
• An entry holds its place from the cycle its read is issued until its visit uses it (a GROUP entry: until its group ends); that place is the credit.

• A table read is a round trip of 2·L_ts + 1 cycles (L_ts = ts_engine_latency each way, one in the memory), so ag_lookahead = 2·L_ts + 2 keeps both queues full whenever every group lasts at least 2 cycles: 4
at the default. Back-to-back one-visit groups would need 4·L_ts + 3, since each STREAM read waits for its GROUP entry; no group of the sort is that short.

• Groups start one per cycle: a zero-length group (R = 0, gap 0) takes one cycle. A group start or visit waiting for its entries waits the same on every tile, since the reads depend only on the tables and

ts_engine_latency: that wait is part of the timetable, not lateness, and at ag_lookahead's bound it doesn't happen [meas: meshsim]. Only an SRAM read queue refusal makes a tile late: the drift condition

• Start begins the readers. A group run's first request goes out once group start's GROUP entry and its first STREAM entry are in: two round trips: 4·L_ts + 3 cycles after the start store (4·L_ts + 2 after
the cycle the start takes effect); a stream run's after one: 2·L_ts + 2 (2·L_ts + 1). A stream run uses only the STREAM reader and queue, and is ready at once.
• Nothing is written back: STREAM and GROUP stay as the controller wrote them, so groups can share streams and a run can be repeated.
GROUP head, valid; STREAM head, valid
junction (lines that cross without a dot don't connect)
Two readers walk the tables ahead of the timetable: GROUP entries in group order, STREAM entries in visit order (each group's streams, R times over).
Two queues of ag_lookahead entries absorb the tables' round trip. The visit side (figure 6.4) pops them and returns a credit for each entry.
